Once all marks are correct, click Submit. Note: Do not navigate away from the roll page before submitting. Leaving without clicking Submit will lose all marks and will require taking the roll again.

Use Felix, the built-in AI assistant, to mark attendance faster by typing a simple instruction instead of marking each student individually. Felix interprets your request, pre-fills attendance statuses, and waits for your review and submission. Click Attendance in the top navigation bar, then click the class block you want to take attendance for. Click the Felix panel icon on the right side of the screen to open the AI assistant. Type your attendance instruction in the chat. Examples: Mark all present Mark all present except [student name] Mark all present except [student name] and [student name] Mark [student name] and [student name] absent Felix pre-fills the attendance status for all relevant students and displays them in a table inside the chat panel. Use the arrow (►) to scroll through the full student list. Review the pre-filled marks. To correct an individual student's mark, click their current status icon to cycle through the available options (Present, Absent, Late to class) until the correct status is shown. Note: Read-only records set by attendance administrators cannot be overridden by Felix. Click Submit in the Felix panel. Felix confirms: "Student attendance updated successfully." Note: The marks now appear on the class roll page. Review the class roll table to confirm all marks are correct (including any manual adjustments). Click Submit on the class roll page.

Use Felix to quickly identify students with specific alerts across your current class or all your classes today. Ask about learning, medical, custody, wellbeing alerts, or upcoming birthdays. Note: Felix uses different time periods based on the request: No class mentioned = your current or next class today Specific class name = most recent data for that class this week Birthdays = this week or next week only (no monthly or yearly queries) Click Attendance in the top navigation bar, then click the class block you want to open. Click the Felix panel icon on the right side of the screen to open the AI assistant. Type your request in the chat. Examples: Show students with learning alerts in this class. Are there any medical plans I should know about for this lesson? Identify learning alerts for all my classes. Show students with custody plans. Review the view-only table showing matching students, their profile image, and class name. Note: If no matches, Felix confirms no results. To view full profile, click student's name in the table.
documents.s: Show list of students in class by filter

documents.t: Use Felix to correct submitted attendance records. Felix displays the class roll for the relevant period so you can update incorrect marks and resubmit. Click Attendance in the top navigation bar, then click the class block you want to correct. Click the Felix panel icon on the right side of the screen to open the AI assistant. Type your correction request. Examples: I need to make a correction in attendance. Fix attendance from yesterday. Correct a mistake on attendance from last week. Review the class roll table showing current attendance marks for the relevant period. To correct a student's mark, click their current status icon to cycle through the available options (Present, Absent, Late to class) until the correct status is shown. Once all corrections are made, click Submit. Felix confirms: The student's attendance has been updated successfully. Refresh the page to see corrected records in the class roll.

StaffXP automatically prompts you to complete any outstanding attendance. The reminder appears as a modal and blocks navigation until the relevant roll has been submitted. The attendance reminder modal appears automatically when you sign in with unsubmitted attendance from a previous session, or when you refresh the page or move to another page, and a past or current class still has not been submitted. Note: The timing of the reminder is configured by attendance admin administrator. The modal shows the class name and the message: “Attendance has not been taken. Please take a moment to complete your attendance roll for today.” The modal locks the screen, so you cannot navigate to any other area of StaffXP. There is no close button. Click Take attendance. The correct class roll opens directly so you can mark and submit the roll. Click the button in the toast message to open the next class with unsubmitted attendance. Note: Repeat this step until all attendance has been submitted.

Click Attendance in the top navigation bar. Scroll down to the table and click Class rolls. Review the table, which shows the following information for each class: Class name ‐ sorted alphabetically by default Teacher ‐ the full name of the assigned teacher Year ‐ the year group #of students ‐ the total number of students enrolled in the class Action ‐ a View roll link to open the class attendance page To filter by date range, set the Start date and End date fields at the top of the table. Click Reset to clear the filters. Note: The table defaults to the current week when it first loads. To search by teacher name, type the name in the Search Teacher field. To search across all columns, click the Search icon above the table and enter your search term (e.g., Science, Mathematics). To view the attendance roll for a specific class, click View roll in the Action column. The class attendance page opens.
documents.s: Leader access to any class roll

documents.t: Use this feature to follow up on students with unresolved absences or late arrivals by contacting the parent directly. Click Attendance in the top navigation bar. Scroll down to the table and click Unresolved attendance tab. Note: The table displays all students with unresolved absences or late arrivals, showing their name, year group, status, session, and primary contact. Find the student you want to action, then click the ** ⋮ button** in the Action column to select an option. To contact a parent, click Contact parent: Copy the parent's phone number using the Copy icon Call the parent using the preferred phone. To email a parent, click Email parent: Your default email client opens with the To: field already filled with the parent’s email address. Enter your subject and message, then send the email.

Use this feature to monitor unresolved attendance records across your school from the start of the school year. Records stay on this page until they are resolved by recording a reason or updating the attendance status. Click Attendance in the top navigation bar. Scroll down to the table and click Unresolved attendance tab. The table displays all students with unresolved absences or late arrivals, showing their name, year group, status, session, primary contact, and action. To search for a specific student, click the Search icon at the top of the table. To filter the table, click the Filter icon, select one or more of the following criteria, then click Apply filters: Year ‐ filter by year group Status ‐ filter by Late or Absent Note: Click Reset filters to clear selected options. Use the pagination controls at the bottom of the table to move between pages. Note: Once a record is resolved, it is automatically removed from this table and moved to the Resolved requests tab.
documents.s: Unresolved absent and late attendance tracking

documents.t: Use this feature to update or correct attendance records for any class within the current term. As an Attendance Officer, you can override submitted attendance records at any time without being restricted by the attendance period lock. Click Attendance in the top navigation bar. Scroll down to the table and click Class rolls tab and find the class you want to update. Click View roll in the Action column. The class role open in edit mode. To navigate to a past date within the current term, click the Attendance date field and select the relevant date. Find the student whose attendance you need to update and click the More options button in their row under the relevant period column. Select the correct status: For Present and Absent, the Select category modal opens. Choose the most appropriate category from the dropdown, then click Save. For Late, the Select category modal opens with Late as the only available category. Click Save to confirm. Once all updates are made, click Submit. Note: The system sends all updated statuses and categories to the backend and a confirmation toast message appears. When a teacher views the class roll after the update, they can hover over the updated attendance icon to see a tooltip showing the original category, the new attendance status and category, and the name of the Attendance Officer who made the change. The teacher can click the updated icon to open a popup showing the student's name, date range, and reason for absence details. Note: The tooltip and popup only appear on records that have been updated by an Attendance Officer.
documents.s: Manual attendance admin update attendance records

documents.t: Use this feature to view attendance requests that have been approved or denied by the Attendance Officer since the start of the school year. This is a read-only view, so no further actions can be taken on resolved records. Click Attendance in the top navigation bar. Scroll down to the table and click Resolved requests tab. The table displays all resolved requests from the start of the school year, with the oldest request at the top. To filter the table, use the dropdown menus at the top to select a Status, Reason, or Year group. Click Reset to clear your selections. Click View details in the Action column for the record you want to review. A modal opens showing: Student name Student ID Reason From and To dates Attachments (supporting files that can be viewed) Note: If a file cannot be opened, an error message appears. If the View details modal cannot be loaded, the message Unable to open view details appears. Use the Previos and Next arrows in the modal to move between resolved requests.

Use the Attendance Overview page to monitor school-wide attendance at a glance. The page displays six summary tiles covering roll reminders, students at risk, attendance trends, today’s attendance, attendance errors, and attendance by category. Click Attendance in the top navigation bar. Review the Roll reminders tile: Shows the total number of classes today where the roll has not been submitted. Shows a percentage change compared with the previous day. Select View all → to see a breakdown by teacher name, class name, period number, and count. Review the Students at risk tile: Shows the total number of students at risk across all classes. Shows a percentage change compared with the previous term. Select View all → to see a list showing student name, student ID, year group, risk category, and current attendance percentage. Review View trends the tile: Provides access to student attendance data by year level, grade level, and attendance category. Select View all → to open the Attendance Trends page. Review the Today's attendance tile: Displays an arc chart showing today’s attendance rate across all classes. Compares today’s attendance with the previous day. Use the ⋮ menu to filter by Present, Absent, or Late. Review the Attendance errors tile. Displays a bar chart showing attendance corrections by source: Parent request, Admin correction, and Teacher correction. Review the Attendance category tile: Displays a bar chart showing attendance by category across all classes. Use the ⋮ menu to filter by category.

Use this page to review and action teacher-submitted attendance correction requests for your assigned year groups. You can approve or deny pending requests, and view previously actioned requests for audit purposes. Click Attendance in the top navigation bar. Scroll down to the table and click Correction request tab. Note: The table displays all correction requests for your assigned year groups, defaulting to the current week. Requests are sorted with Pending first, followed by Approved and Denied, with the most recent requests shown first. To search for a specific request, click the Search icon at the top of the table. To filter the table, use the Date and Status filters. Find the request you want to action and review the relevant details, such as the student, class, date, current code, requested correction, and request status. Use the Action column based on the request status: Pending ‐ select Approve or reject Approved ‐ no available action Rejected ‐ click the comment icon to veiw the rejection reason To approve a request, click Approve in the Action column. The status updates to Approved and a success toast message appears. To reject a request, click Reject in the Action column. A modal opens and asks you to enter a denial reason. Type the reason in the text field, then click Submit. The status updates to Denied and a success toast message appears. Note: The Submit button stays disabled until a reason is entered. If the system is unable to update the status, the message Unable to approve/deny this request status appears. Try again or contact your administrator. Note: After an Attendance Officer actions a correction request, teachers see the updated attendance status in the class roll in real time. Hovering over the icon shows the original category, the updated status, and who made the change. The tooltip appears only for records updated by an Attendance Officer and also in the attendance summary view.
documents.s: Attendance admin view teacher correction request (WIP)

documents.t: The Attendance Officer can access class rolls for the year groups assigned to their role. The steps for accessing and navigating class rolls are the same as for a Leader. For full steps, refer to Leader Access to Any Class Roll. Note: If a class roll does not appear in your Class rolls tab, it may belong to a year group outside your assigned scope. Contact your administrator to review your year group assignment.
documents.s: Attendance admin access any class roll

documents.t: Use this page to track attendance trends across your classes, identify students at risk, and analyse absence patterns by timing and day. The page combines summary tiles, visual charts, and an individual student attendance table to give you a complete view of attendance performance. Click Attendance in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar, click View details → under Attendance analytics. The Attendance Analytics page opens. Check the alert banner at the top of the page: If any students have fallen below the 85% attendance threshold, the banner shows the number of flagged students. Click View flagged students to open a modal showing each student’s name, ID, year group, risk category, and current attendance percentage. Click Close to dismiss the modal. Note: Felix AI generates the flagged students list based on the attendance threshold set by your school. Review the three summary tiles below the alert banner: Attendance rate ‐ the overall attendance rate across your classes, compared to the previous term. Absent today ‐ the number of students absent today, compared to yesterday. Late arrivals ‐ the total number of late arrivals, compared to the previous term. Use the By class dropdown on the right to filter all charts by a specific class, or leave it set to All classes. Review the three charts: Attendance trend this term ‐ a line graph showing weekly attendance across the term. Absence timing trends ‐ a bar chart showing when absences most commonly occur, such as Mondays, Fridays, the first day of term, morning, or afternoon. Absence by day ‐ a bar chart showing which days of the week have the highest absence rates. Use the action icons in the top-right corner of each chart: List icon (≡) ‐ view the chart data as a table. Expand icon (⤢) ‐ view the chart in fullscreen. ⋮ menu ‐ export the chart data as CSV, PNG, or JPG. Scroll down to the table section to view students' details. Use the Search students field above the table to find a specific student. The table updates dynamically as you type. Use the pagination controls at the bottom of the table to move between pages.

When an emergency is triggered, the Navigation bar will turn red. All options on the dashboard will be automatically disabled. An Emergency roll screen will appear. To the left of the Staff XP icon, there are dropdown menus for Attendance and for a Muster Coordinator or Emergency Coordinator (if applicable). Below the Emergency roll list, there is a space to add Students not on roll. There is a search bar with a dropdown to add any student in your care who is not on the roll. During an emergency, Felix is disabled, all attendance must be done manually.

Use this page to review emergency attendance performance data across all past emergencies. The dashboard shows how quickly classes were cleared, how fast teachers marked attendance, and a breakdown of emergencies by type and term. This page is available to Leaders, Emergency Coordinators, and Muster Coordinators. Click the hamburger menu (☰) in the left corner of the navigation bar. Select Emergency analytics to open the page. Review the two summary tiles at the top of the page: Avg time to clear classes ‐ shows the average time it took all classes to complete their emergency roll, with a trend indicator and percentage change compared to the last emergency Avg time to mark attendance ‐ shows the average time it took teachers to mark emergency attendance, with a trend indicator and percentage change compared to the last emergency Note: A green upward arrow indicates the metric has improved. A red downward arrow indicates it has worsened. Review the two charts below the tiles: Emergency per term ‐ shows the trend of the total number of emergencies across each term over time Emergency per term by type ‐ shows the count of each emergency type (e.g., Drill, Fire, Gas leak) for the current term Scroll down to the Emergency table to view all the past emergency events for the current academic year, most recent first: Reason ‐ the type of emergency Date ‐ the date the emergency occurred Clear time ‐ the time it took to clear all classes Report ‐ a report link to open the emergency details page for that event To filter the table by emergency type, click the Filter icon. Select one or more emergency types, then click Apply filters. Click Reset filters to clear your selection and return to the default view. To search for a specific emergency, click the Search icon above the table. To open a full emergency report, click Full report in the Report column for the event you want to review. Review the summary tiles on the Emergency Details page: Avg time to clear classes shows the average time it took all classes to complete their emergency roll for that event. Avg time to mark attendance shows the average time it took teachers to mark emergency attendance. Avg time to clear muster points shows the average time it took coordinators to clear all muster points. Note: Each tile includes a trend indicator and percentage change compared to the previous emergency. Review the Emergency attendance table showing the time taken by each teacher to mark emergency attendance for their class. Use the Search icon to find a specific student. Click Print icon to print the table. Review the Comparing daily and emergency attendance panel on the right side of the page: Marked absent ‐ present at emergency shows students who were marked absent in their regular roll but were accounted for during the emergency. Marked present ‐ absent at emergency shows students who were marked present in their regular roll but were missing during the emergency. Scroll down to the Muster points table which includes muster points, coordinator, and time taken. Use the Search icon to find a specific muster point. Click the Print icon to print the table.

In an emergency, the Navigation bar will go red. The Attendance page will open automatically. At the safety point, you can take attendance. Find the Emergency roll column. This is prefilled with attendance from earlier. Absent students will be marked with a note. Go through the list and confirm each student is found (this is represented by a white circle with a check mark). For found students, no action is needed. To identify a missing student, click on the white circle, which will allow you to change the status to Missing. The symbol will change to a red circle with a grey x. Next to each circle, there is an area to add notes per student.

Five minutes after the first emergency attendance, a pop-up window will appear prompting you to update the status of students listed as missing. This prompt only appears if students are recorded as Missing. Each student, with a profile picture, name and their grade level, is listed in a table. Next to each student, there are three action options: Add note (100 characters) Missing Found Even if you added a note, you need to select either Missing or Found. Note: Selecting Missing or Found causes the student to be hidden from the list. When all the students in your class are reported found, a success message appears saying "All students in your class have been found."
documents.s: Reminder: update missing student status - Teacher

documents.t: During an emergency, it is possible to print out the class attendance list. Note: Online emergency attendance must still be completed. Above the Emergency roll column, there are three icons. Click the Printer icon. The print menu will open, with a table of the class list in the preview. Check the printer number and other details. Press Print
documents.s: Print current class attendance during emergency

documents.t: Note: During an emergency, the screen automatically changes to emergency attendance. Next to each name in the Emergency roll column, click Add note. A pop-up will appear. Type in the Notes about student text box. Click Add note at the bottom right of the pop-up. The Note will appear below the student's name, with the date and time.
Scroll to the end of the emergency attendance list to the Students not on roll section. In the search bar, type the student's full name. Click Add.

Note: If requesting an activity at a new off-site location, Request a venue before completing the activity request. Click Extra curricular in the Navigation bar. Click Create extra-curricular activity → in the Request an extra-curricular activity tile. Complete the Activity details, starting with General information. Complete the Venue details.
Click Sign in with Microsoft. Use GEMS M365 login account details (email and password). Click Sign in.

The Navigation bar runs across the top of the screen at all times. Click on any of the headings or navigation links to access the relevant page. StaffXP is the landing, home page, also known as the MyDay page. On the far left, there is a menu icon where there are links to Training, Reporting and Administration. To the right of StaffXP, there are navigation links for Attendance, Notices, Wellbeing and Extra curricular. At the far right of the screen, there are icons for Search, Notifications and User menu. The Search icon opens up a search bar to search for pages or students. The Notifications bell icon opens up into a menu, and is organised into Messages or Alerts. Under the User icon, a menu appears where you can change the theme, view your profile, edit settings or sign out.

The Attendance page allows teachers and admin staff to track attendance for a single school day or within a week. For Teachers: Navigate to the Attendance page by clicking the navigation link/ tab in the Navigation bar. Teachers will be able to track attendance for their classes. The classes appear as a list in the calendar schedule. Above the calendar, there is a display of today's date. There are arrow keys to change the date. On the top-right corner of the schedule panel, use the Day / Week dropdown to switch between Day and Week view. On the left of the screen are tiles for information on Late students, Unexcused absences, and Absent students on assessment days. There is a small tile to View analytics. For Administrators/School Leaders: 1.

The Notices page displays upcoming and relevant notices to you. You can create and manage notices, and filter them by your interests. Navigate to the Notices page, through the Navigation bar. There are options to Manage notices or Create notice. Along the top-right of the screen is a dropdown menu to select relevant Interests by category. Featured notices appear per day. The interests are displayed below the featured notices as tiles. They can also be viewed by filtering into categories.

You can plan for school activities and manage resources on the Activities page. Here you can review a shared calendar to see when other planned activities are taking place and what resources they require, to avoid conflicts and ensure resource availability. Select Activities from the Navigation bar. There are three tiles running across the top of the page: Request venue, Calendar view and Request activity. Note: Click the text or arrow on the lower right of each tile to navigate to another page to complete the request. In the navigation bar below the tiles: Your requests: this shows a list of pending or approved activity requests. Booking status: this provides a list of the resource bookings and the required quantities. All venues: is a list of approved or previously visited venues for school activities. Parent volunteers: includes a list of all the parent volunteers who could support with school activities. Note: Each of these tabs has a filter and search option.

This is the main space to monitor and support student wellbeing. Here you can create and track wellbeing notes. There are several wellbeing metrics that display the different category trends of wellbeing notes.

This is the landing page for all extra-curricular activities. Here, you can plan, browse, and create new extra-curricular activities. There is a calendar to track all activities and their dates. Click the Extra-curricular tab in the Navigation bar. There are two tiles below the heading. Request an extra-curricular activity allows you to request the creation of a new extracurricular activity. Extra-curricular calendar displays a calendar of when different activities occur. Below the tiles, there is a small navigation bar with tabs for Your request, Booking status, Supervising activities and Staffing to follow up and track activities. Each tab has a search and filter function to streamline searches.

MyDay is the platform's main landing page and homescreen. When in other pages, return to the MyDay page by clicking the Staff XP tab in the Navigation bar. The MyDay tiles display information relevant to the day, including Today's schedule, Assignments to mark and a To-Do list. You can also view notices, this week's birthdays, and open wellbeing tasks. Also, there is a Quick links tile for quick access to Employee self-service, Topics and FAQs, and to View markbook.
The MyDay landing page changes appearance throughout the day to match the time of day the teacher is using the platform.

Running lengthways on the left side of the screen is Today's schedule. There is a list with the task, timing, and location. There is a blue line indicator on the left of the list to show which task is active. After the task's time has passed, the dashed outline of the circle becomes solid blue, with a blue check mark in the middle.

The timetable of classes for today shows as a banner running across the screen. There is a red line indicator to mark the time and the active class. After the class time has passed, the text fades to grey and the word DONE appears next to the time.
Daily updates from the school canteen show in the Canteen specials tile. The tile displays the dish name, whether it is hot or cold, whether it is a snack, and each dish's price.
The To do list tile links to Microsoft ToDo. It shows a summary of upcoming tasks and their due dates.

The Professional learning tile shows the number of hours of professional learning in a pie chart by category. Below the pie chart is a breakdown of the different professional learning categories, along with completion or planned dates.
Employee Self-Service (ESS) is an area where the user can... Click Employee self-service in the Quick links tile to access the page.

The User Menu is where you can personalise the platform to best suit your needs and optimise workflow. Click the User button (shaped like the silhouette of a person). A dropdown menu will show options to change the Theme (from light to dark mode), a Profile section, Settings and the option to Sign Out.

The Theme settings affect screen displays. Light mode uses a light background with dark text. Dark mode shows a dark background with light text. Subtle light and subtle dark are tones between light and dark. It may be easier to use light mode in bright light and dark mode in dim light. However, this is entirely up to the user's preferences and comfort. Click the User icon. The dropdown menu will show four boxes in a row below the heading Theme, showing light to dark mode. Select the option, and the change will occur instantly.

In the Settings, you can manage the appearance of your platform according to your preferences. You can also manage accessibility and whether to receive push notifications. Click the User icon ▸ Settings. There are two tabs below Appearance, Theme and Font size. To change the Theme, click on the dropdown arrow. You can select between Light, subtle light, subtle dark and Dark. Selecting the dropdown menu below the Font size heading allows you to choose between Small, Medium or Large fonts. These will reflect throughout the platform. Accessibility has on/off toggles for High contrast mode and Reduced motion. Enable or disable push notifications in Notifications with an on/off toggle. After making any changes to the settings, an option to Save changes or Cancel appears at the top right of the screen.

Your Profile page contains all your personal, professional, and work information. The top banner displays your profile picture and job title. Click the User icon. Selecting Profile from the dropdown reveals three tiles of information on the page. On the left, there is Personal Information, first and last names, and date of birth. The middle tile shows Professional Information, as your work email address. On the right tile, there is Work Information, including job title, company name and office location.

To log out or sign out means to successfully close or end your session on the device. You will need to sign in again with your credentials after signing out. It is recommended to log out of your account if multiple users are on the same computer. Click the User icon. Scroll to the last option on the dropdown and click Sign Out. This will automatically return you to the sign-in page.

These are found in the Settings section of the User menu. There are options to toggle each setting on/off. High contrast mode is a feature to support users with visual difficulties or impairments. Here, the colours change, and the platform interfaces are simplified to maximise legibility. Reduced motion mode minimises or reduces animations throughout the platform. This feature is designed to reduce eye strain, headaches, and motion sickness for users with vestibular disorders.

Featured notices appear above all the other notices. There is a yellow star on the top right of the thumbnail image. Featured notices are important or urgent and require attention. Featured notices will only appear while they are active. If the notice's active time has elapsed, it will no longer appear in the featured area. In the Notices tab, click Manage notices. Scroll down to Notices below the two tiles. Use the Search or Filter functions to find the notice (if needed). Click the star icon (☆) in the Action column on the right of the screen. The icon will fill to a solid blue, and a pop-up message will appear: Featured updated. This notice is now featured. To remove a notice from the featured banner, click the solid star icon (★). A confirmation message appears: Featured updated. This notice is no longer featured.
documents.s: Set a notice to be featured

documents.t: This feature allows you to customise and view the Notices types most relevant to you first. These appear under the Your interests tab. In the Notices page, there is a navigation bar below the heading. To the right, there is a filter icon to filter the notices as needed. Right of the icon is an Interests dropdown menu. Select the category or categories as required. (General, Arts, Community, Cultural, Sport). The page will update immediately. Note: All notices can still be viewed under their corresponding tabs.

In the Notices tab, click Manage notices. Click on the number on the Active Notices tile to see all active published notices. Scroll down to Notices below the two tiles. There is a list of user-created notices. Use the Search or Filter functions to find the notice (if needed).
In the Notices tab, click Manage notices. Scroll down to Notices below the two tiles. There is a list of user-created notices. Use the Search or Filter functions to find the notice (if needed).

Notices are announcements you publish to staff, parents, and/or students. Creating one is a short wizard: enter the details, choose the audience, set the visibility window, then review and publish. Open the notice form Click Notices in the navigation bar, then click Create notice + in the top-right corner. Fill in the notice details Complete the Notice details in the pop-up window: A Notice title The Notice category (from the dropdown) A Notice description Optional: a thumbnail image, whether an RSVP is required, the date and time, a Reference link title and Reference link, and a supporting document Then click Next. Note: Thumbnail images and supporting documents must meet the accepted file size and format. Choose the audience In the Audience type section, select who can see the notice — Staff, Parents, or Students. Under Select staff, pick the relevant staff, and under Year groups, choose the year groups it applies to. Click Next. Note: If the notice is going to parents, make sure it complies with your school's communication guidelines. Set the visibility In the Visibility tab, fill in the From and Until fields — the notice is visible to your audience during this window. Choose whether it should repeat, then click Next. Review and publish In the Review and Publish tab, check the details and tone. To change anything, click Back. When everything is correct, click Publish.

Update a notice you've already created — its details, audience, or visibility. Note: You can only edit a notice that you created. Open Manage notices In the Notices tab, click Manage notices (①) in the top-right corner. Find your notice On the Manage notices page, find it in the Your notices list (②) — filter with the Active notices and Scheduled notices tiles if it helps — then click that notice's edit icon (③). Open the section to edit In the Edit notice details window, expand the section you want to change — Details, Audience type, or Visibility (④). Make your changes and save Edit the fields as needed (⑤), then click Save changes (⑥).

Notifications are brief, timely alerts that the platform pushes to your device to provide updates, reminders, or messages. These notifications share information quickly and help maintain planning and organisation. The notifications on the StaffXP page are categorised into Messages, Alerts, and Favourites. You can view each category by clicking on the tab heading in the dropdown. Clicking on a notification automatically takes you to the relevant section.

Notifications can be found on the right side of the Navigation bar. New or unread notifications will appear as a white number in a red bubble at the top right of the bell icon. You can view notifications in the dropdown menu, or click any notification to expand the menu into a Notification centre web page with the same category headings (Messages, Alerts, Favourites).

To access notifications, click the bell icon. A dropdown will open up. The notifications are divided into three categories, Messages, Alerts and Favourites. There is a bubble with the number of notifications in each category to the right of each heading. Clicking on each heading opens the corresponding tab. Note: When a tab is active, it is underlined in blue, and the notification bubble changes from grey to pink. Unread messages appear with a solid blue square on the right. Beneath each notification message, there is a time when the message was sent, an option to Mark as read, and a heart icon to favourite the notification. At the bottom of the dropdown menu, there are options to View all messages or Mark all as read. Clicking on View all messages opens the notification centre.

This is a full-size web page for viewing any notifications. Navigate to the Notification Centre. Click the bell icon ▸ View all messages. The notifications are still divided by category, Messages, Alerts, and Favourites. Clicking each tab will display the notifications for that category. Below the tab headings, there is a set of filter buttons to view All messages, Unread messages or Read messages. There is a search option on the right side of the screen. Notification messages appear in a list with a grey background for each message. Unread messages have a solid blue square on the left. Click the vertical ellipsis on the right of the message frame to Mark as read, Mark as favourite or Delete. In the top right corner of the screen, there are buttons for Mark all as read and Clear all.

In the alerts dropdown or the notification centre, the Alerts tab is the central tab. Click the tab to view the Alerts. There are different categories of alerts, including environmental and weather warnings, transport disruptions, security notices, and health advisories. The category of each alert is displayed when you receive the alert.

Navigate to the notification centre by clicking the bell icon ▸ Alerts tab. Click the Create alert + button in the top right corner. A pop-up window will appear; fill in the required fields. Enter an alert Title. Select a Category from the dropdown menu. Add a Description for the alert. Click Submit in the bottom right corner. Note: You can only click Submit when all the required fields in the pop-up are complete.

This is the landing page for all messages, alerts and favourites. The messages will appear in a list; each message is framed with a grey background. Unread messages have a solid blue square on the left. On the landing page, there is a filter to toggle between All, Unread and Read messages. Along the right, there is a search function. Navigate to the Notification Centre. Click the bell icon ▸ View all messages. The Notifications page will automatically open. Clicking on a message will direct you to the corresponding page. For example: Clicking on a message related to activities will open the activities page. Click on the vertical ellipsis on the right of the message frame to Mark as read, Mark as favourite or Delete. In the top right corner of the screen, there are buttons for Mark all as read and Clear all.
Push notifications are short, clickable alerts sent directly from an app or web browser to your laptop. You can choose whether to receive push notifications.

Mark important messages as favourites to access and view them more easily later. There are two ways to mark a message as favourite: Click the bell icon. In the dropdown, each message has a black heart icon outline on the right. Click the outline and the heart will fill in a solid black colour. This message is now marked as favourite. At the bottom of the dropdown menu, select View all messages. To the right of each message box, click the vertical ellipsis. Select Mark as favourite from the dropdown menu.

Note: A message must be marked as a favourite to be viewed under the Favourites tab. There are different ways to view favourite messages: Click the bell icon. In the dropdown, select the Favourites tab to view the most recent favourite messages. At the bottom of the menu, click View all favourites to open the Notification centre page. Or: Click on View all messages ▸ Favourites.

When you assign a wellbeing task to yourself, or if another member of staff assigns you to a wellbeing task, this will appear as a message in your notifications. Click the bell icon. In the dropdown, the message will appear with the heading New wellbeing task assigned. The task Title will appear in blue in the message. Click the Title. This will automatically open the Wellbeing note. You can view the task in more detail by clicking on it in the Tasks tile. Click the pencil icon in the task; this will open a pop-up window. Update the task Status in the appropriate field from selecting either Open, Completed or Canceled. Note: Selecting Completed or Canceled in the status will permanently remove the task.
documents.s: Notification — assigned a wellbeing case task

documents.t: If a Wellbeing case that you are assigned to is resolved or cancelled by another member of staff. You will receive a message in your notifications. Click the bell icon. In the dropdown, the message will appear with the heading Wellbeing case resolved or Wellbeing case cancelled. The note Title appears in blue in the message. Click the Title to open the Wellbeing note. The status in the top right corner will be updated to either Canceled or Resolved.

In the Navigation bar, click the notifications bell icon. At the bottom of the dropdown menu, you can toggle Push notifications on or off. Note: You may have to check your browser security settings to ensure you can receive push notifications.
Version: v1

Student wellbeing encompasses all aspects of a student's life, including happiness and health, academic challenges, and social relationships at home and at school. The wellbeing landing page is an area to monitor and support student wellbeing.

Click on the Wellbeing tab to open the Wellbeing landing page. On the left tile below the heading, click Create wellbeing note →. Fill in the required fields (indicated by an asterisk *) in the pop-up window. Add a Title for the wellbeing note. Enter the Student name (you can type or select the name from the dropdown menu). Add a Description. Select a Note type (choose one of the seven subcategories). Under Sentiment, identify if the note is Positive or Negative. Identify the Priority for action (Low, Medium, High or Critical). Note: The student ID and year group will automatically populate. Attach photos if required. If this wellbeing note is related to an existing note, you can connect the notes in Linked note by typing the start of the heading of the note you wish to link to, and the content will autofill. In the Notify staff member text, start typing a staff member's name to share the wellbeing note with other staff members. Note: A dropdown will open so you can select the staff member without typing the full name. Click the blue square outline with a + in the centre to add more staff members. Select if parents need to be notified of this wellbeing note. Select Publish note. Note: The note can only be published if all the required fields are completed.

Click on the Wellbeing tab to open the Wellbeing landing page. On the left tile below the heading, click Create wellbeing note →. Fill in the required fields (indicated by an asterisk *) in the pop-up window. Below the Upload optional photos or documents heading, click Choose file. Note: The total maximum file size is 10MB. A File folder will pop up, select the relevant document. Select Open. The file will automatically upload. You can add as many files as long as you remain below the maximum file size. To remove a file, press the X on the right of the file heading. Save by clicking Publish note. Note: The note can only be published if all the required fields are completed.

Navigate to the Wellbeing landing page from the Navigation bar. Click Track and resolve notes → on the right tile below the heading. Select the relevant Wellbeing note from the Active notes tab. Select the blue square with a + sign on the Tasks tile on the right. A pop-up window will open up. Complete the required fields marked with an asterisk (*). Add a Title. Select an Assignee. Add Notes to describe the task. Click Save. Note: The task will automatically appear in the tasks tile. Edit the task by clicking on the pencil icon. In the pop-up window, there is a Status bar to update and monitor the task status.

After you submit a wellbeing note, you will get a pop-up notification at the top right of the window confirming the success of the note submission. Changing the status of a note will also result in a pop-up notification. Note: If a linked member of staff makes any edits to the note, the changes will appear as notifications in the dropdown below the Bell icon or in the Notification centre.

When you successfully create a wellbeing note, it automatically opens a case. The steps below outline how to find Active notes. In the Wellbeing tab, select Track and resolve notes → on the right tile below the heading. Below Case Title is a list of all the Active notes. Click the tab subheading Closed/resolved notes to view previous or currently inactive notes.

In situations where more than one student is involved in a wellbeing case, or more relevant notes are required, it is possible to connect a new Wellbeing note to an existing note. Check the title of the existing note(s) beforehand for linking. Navigate to the Wellbeing landing page. Click Create wellbeing note → on the left tile. Complete the mandatory fields in the pop-up window. In the Linked note field, begin typing the heading of the relevant wellbeing note. There is a dropdown that will share all the notes containing the same words. Select the correct note; it is now linked. To add more linked notes, press the blue square with the white +. To remove an empty linked note space, click on the red waste bin icon. Note: To unlink a linked note, press the X at the end of the search field.

Navigate to the Wellbeing landing page. Click Track and resolve notes → on the tile on the right. In the Active notes tab, find and select the relevant wellbeing note. The note will automatically open, where you can view: Student name and number Note description Note type Sentiment Staff Notified Below the area is an AI-generated summary of the note and details. There are also tiles for Comment timeline and follow-up Tasks related to the note.
documents.s: View details of a wellbeing case

documents.t: Navigate to the Wellbeing landing page. Click Track and resolve notes → on the tile on the right. In the Active notes tab, find and select the relevant wellbeing note. Note: Confirm that there are no outstanding tasks or follow-up required on the wellbeing note. Once a note is resolved or closed, it cannot be opened again. A separate note will be needed. After selecting the note, the Update status box will become blue. Click the Update status box. A pop-up will appear. From the dropdown, you can select Active, Resolved or Cancelled. Click submit, the status will automatically update.

As the wellbeing situation evolves, or more information becomes available, it is possible to add supplementary comments to the existing wellbeing note. Navigate to the relevant note from the Wellbeing landing page ▸ Track my notes. Select the relevant note. In the middle Comments tile, click the +. Fill in the fields for the comment. Upload supporting documents if required. Click Save. To edit an existing comment, press the pencil icon to edit the note.

For each Wellbeing note, you can assign follow-up tasks for yourself or other members of staff. One member of staff can be assigned per task. Navigate to the relevant note from the Wellbeing landing page ▸ Track and resolve notes →. Select the relevant note. Click the blue square with the white + on the Tasks tile on the right of the screen. A pop-up window will open to Add new task. Complete the fields. Add a Title. Select an Assignee. Start typing the name, and all the names, including those characters, will appear in a dropdown. Add Notes. Click Save. The save button will only be enabled when all fields are completed. The task will appear in the Tasks tile on the right. Note: After successfully saving, a pop-up message will appear in the top-right corner confirming the addition of the task. To edit the task or update the status, click on the Pencil icon. Another pop-up window will open. This window will have an additional field, Status. Update the task status by selecting either Open, Completed or Canceled. Click Save. Another pop-up message will confirm successful saving. Note: Changing the status to Completed or Canceled will permanently remove the task from the Tasks tile.

Navigate to the Wellbeing landing page. Click Track and resolve notes → on the tile on the right. In the Active notes tab, find and select the relevant wellbeing note. The page displays a description and details of the wellbeing note. Below, with a grey background, on the left, there is an AI-generated Summary of the wellbeing note and details. Note: The text box expands to adjust to the amount of text present, there is no need to click the information box.
